description: I enjoy exploring new ideas, stepping beyond my comfort zone, and embracing challenges that contribute to both my personal and professional growth. I'm naturally curious about how technology can be leveraged to address real-world challenges and transform ideas into meaningful, practical solutions.
summary:
How It Addresses the Challenge

Terrestrial 1g medical ranges are clinically invalid in weightlessness. The journal assesses telemetry across 10 anatomical systems using the Three-Reference Adaptation Model—evaluating vitals against Earth 1g norms, expected in-flight 0g adaptation envelopes, and individual rolling baselines. It pairs an interactive anatomical body map with a Predictive Decompensation Forecast Engine (least-squares regression detecting early SANS optic disc thickening days in advance), a multi-system readiness index (82%, 95% CI: 77%–87%), and four-tiered clinical decision support enforcing a strict non-pharmacologic mandate (zero drug dosing).

Why It Is Important

During deep-space exploration, speed-of-light radio latency reaches up to 24 minutes one-way (48 minutes round-trip), making real-time telemedicine from Earth flight control impossible during acute physiological shifts. By transitioning spaceflight health from reactive ground consultation to autonomous, predictive in-cabin monitoring, the system empowers crews to detect subtle physiological drift and initiate physical countermeasures before clinical decompensation threatens mission success.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

The Orbital Field Medical Journal is an offline-first, zero-dependency clinical decision-support Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to provide autonomous physiological self-assessment for astronauts during long-duration spaceflight missions.

  • Three-Reference Adaptation Model: Terrestrial 1g medical norms fail in weightlessness. The system assesses 10 anatomical organ systems across three concurrent reference envelopes:
    1. Earth 1g Sea-Level Range (terrestrial baseline context),
    2. In-Flight 0g Adaptation Envelope (expected healthy microgravity remodeling per NASA-STD-3001), and
    3. Astronaut Personal Baseline (individual rolling 14-day pre-flight and in-flight mean).
  • Predictive Decompensation Forecast Engine: Instead of triggering reactive alarms after tissue injury occurs, the engine performs least-squares linear regression over longitudinal historical epochs (e.g., Mission Days 15–19). For Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), it calculates a cephalad fluid velocity of +4.5 μm/day+4.5\,\mu\text{m/day}+4.5μm/day (R2=0.997R^2 = 0.997R2=0.997, SE=0.48 μmSE = 0.48\,\mu\text{m}SE=0.48μm) and projects that peripapillary retinal swelling will breach the 335 μm335\,\mu\text{m}335μm Flight Surgeon Review Threshold in approximately 2 days (Mission Day 21).
  • Weighted Multi-System Readiness Engine: Synthesizes telemetry across all 10 anatomical systems into a calibrated composite readiness index (82.0%82.0\%82.0%, 95% CI: 77%–87%95\%\text{ CI: } 77\%–87\%95% CI: 77%–87%). Catastrophic sensor inputs strictly enforce an immediate crisis floor cap (≤35%\le 35\%≤35%), preventing fit-for-duty false positives.
  • 4-Stage Incident Escalation: During acute events (such as the simulated Day 19 SANS breach), the system executes an automated 4-step triage chain: metric ingestion →\rightarrow→ microgravity pattern classification →\rightarrow→ readiness recalibration →\rightarrow→ non-pharmacologic countermeasure prescription.
  • Single Source of Truth (MissionState): Every statistic, threshold, and countdown timer (synchronized at 38:14) across all UI cards flows reactively from a central state store with zero hardcoded numbers.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates False-Alarm Triage: Accurately differentiates normal physiological adaptation (e.g., non-pathological cephalad fluid redistribution or 3–7 cm spinal elongation) from true pathological decompensation.
  • 48-Hour Proactive Forewarning: By forecasting threshold crossings days before clinical symptoms emerge, crews can initiate corrective physical countermeasures (such as Lower Body Negative Pressure / LBNP) before irreversible optic disc edema occurs.
  • Guaranteed Clinical Safety (Zero Drug Dosing): Strictly avoids autonomous drug prescribing or dosing calculations. Clinical countermeasures are limited strictly to operational, environmental, and physical interventions (e.g., 15° head-up sleep elevation, ambient pCO2pCO_2pCO2​ scrubber checks, ARED resistive exercise).
  • Total Offline Reliability: Operates 100% offline via a versioned cache-first Service Worker (ofmj-v16). Telemetry logs and field notes persist locally in localStorage with memory fallback, ensuring full functionality during communication blackouts.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project directly solves the single greatest medical hurdle of interplanetary human space exploration: speed-of-light communication latency.

  • Between Low Earth Orbit and Mars, radio signals take up to 24 minutes each way (48 minutes round-trip). During acute physiological shifts or progressive deconditioning, astronauts cannot wait an hour for flight surgeons in Houston or Bengaluru to inspect telemetry packets.
  • Orbital Field Medical Journal shifts space medicine from ground-telemedicine dependency to autonomous in-cabin predictive decision-support, safeguarding crew physical longevity, cognitive performance, and mission success on journeys beyond Earth.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages & Web Standards: Native HTML5, modern CSS3 (Custom Properties, CSS Grid, Flexbox), and modular ES6+ JavaScript. Built with zero runtime framework dependencies (no React/Vue/Angular overhead or bloated node_modules).
  • Mathematics & Analytics: Custom pure-JavaScript engines for least-squares linear regression, Exponentially Weighted Moving Averages (EWMA, α=0.3\alpha = 0.3α=0.3), Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) drift detection, and Studentized confidence intervals (95% CI: ±1.96⋅SE95\%\text{ CI: } \pm 1.96 \cdot SE95% CI: ±1.96⋅SE).
  • Offline Architecture & PWA: Cache-First Service Worker API, Web Storage API (localStorage), and Web App Manifest for fullscreen standalone operation on iPads, Android tablets, and laptop workstations.
  • Automated Verification Harness: Standalone, embedded browser test runner (tests.html) featuring 123 automated verification assertions executing natively with zero external test runners.
  • Typography & Ergonomics: Google Fonts (Fraunces high-legibility editorial serif, Inter tabular sans-serif), custom vector SVG medical illustrations, and Microsoft PowerPoint automation via python-pptx.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Editorial-Clinical "Field Journal" Aesthetic: Replaces cold, high-glare, dark sci-fi HUD dashboards with an elegant, warm ivory visual identity inspired by classic medical field journals. This calm editorial tone reduces visual fatigue and psychological anxiety during months in confined metallic habitats.
  • Circadian-Aware "Night Cabin" Protocol: Features a one-click toggle to a melanopic-preserving deep slate/amber night palette, designed to prevent melatonin suppression and circadian rhythm disruption during critical pre-sleep shifts.
  • Multi-Signal Colorblind-Safe Redundancy: Telemetry status is never communicated by color alone. Every status level pairs color with a distinct geometric glyph (● Circle for In-Range, ▲ Triangle for Watch, ◆ Diamond for Flight Surgeon, ⬢ Octagon for Emergency), high-contrast borders, and clear clinical text labels.
  • Interactive Three-Reference Visual Ruler: Reimagines terrestrial laboratory reference bars into an intuitive 3-tier visual ruler showing Earth 1g, In-Flight 0g, and personal rolling baseline simultaneously.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Pressurized Spacesuit Ergonomics: All interactive buttons, tabs, nodes, and steppers enforce minimum 48×48 px48 \times 48\text{ px}48×48 px hit targets with generous touch padding for gloved operation or motor ataxia in weightlessness.
  • Extreme Visual Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA): Contrast ratios reach 13.7:1 (Day Cabin) and 14.2:1 (Night Cabin), far exceeding standard accessibility guidelines. All caption text is locked to a minimum of 13px.
  • Rigorous NASA Evidence Grounding: All normal bands, threshold triggers, and physiological rationales cite strictly 5 authentic NASA Human Research Program publications:
    1. NASA HRP Evidence Report: "Risk of SANS" (hrp.nasa.gov)
    2. NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) (osdr.nasa.gov)
    3. NASA Human Research Roadmap (HRR) (humanresearchroadmap.nasa.gov)
    4. Mader TH et al. (2011), Ophthalmology
    5. NASA Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health (LSAH)
  • Speed-of-Light Operational Realism: Includes an active environment switcher (ISS 0.5s, Lunar Gateway 1.3s, Mars Transit 12.0 min, Surface Hab 24.0 min) that dynamically alters triage guidelines based on physical communication delays.
